title: Datasets & Training Pipelines
description: Study dataset and dataloader responsibilities, collation and variable-length batches, validation loops and metric aggregation, and reproducibility and data leakage checks. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Dataset and DataLoader responsibilities
lessons.description: Describe the data returned by one Dataset item and by one loader batch, including labels and metadata.
lessons.conceptOverview: A Dataset maps an index to an example or yields a stream of examples. DataLoader handles batching, workers, and collation. Keep training-only transformations separate from deterministic validation preprocessing. Do not fit normalization or vocabulary statistics on held-out examples just because the loader can access them.
lessons.whyItMatters: Separate example construction from batching and validation preprocessing.

sections.content: A training loader can shuffle examples and apply random crops. A validation loader should use a reproducible transform so checkpoint comparisons measure model changes rather than random input changes.

lessons.title: Collation and variable-length batches
lessons.description: Construct the padding mask for two sequences and show how masked token loss is normalized by the valid-token count.
lessons.conceptOverview: Collation combines examples into a batch. Variable-length sequences often require padding plus an attention mask or length vector. Padding values must not contribute incorrectly to a loss or average. Bucketing similar lengths can reduce padding waste but changes batching and shuffling decisions.
lessons.whyItMatters: Normalize sequence losses over intended valid tokens rather than arbitrary padding positions.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.content: Sequences of lengths 3 and 7 require 14 padded positions in a rectangular batch, but only 10 represent real tokens. Averaging loss over all 14 without masking changes the objective.

lessons.title: Validation loops and metric aggregation
lessons.description: Compute both aggregation methods for unequal batches and explain which estimates per-example accuracy.
lessons.conceptOverview: Validation should avoid parameter updates and use consistent model behavior. Aggregate metrics at the correct unit: averaging batch means equally biases results when batch sizes differ. Accumulate counts or weighted sums, then compute the dataset-level metric. Keep model selection separate from final test evaluation.
lessons.whyItMatters: Weight batch metrics by example count when computing per-example dataset metrics.

lessons.title: Reproducibility and data leakage checks
lessons.description: Audit a small dataset for duplicate groups and define a group-aware or time-aware split appropriate to the task.
lessons.conceptOverview: Record split definitions, seeds, preprocessing, package versions, and configuration. Seeds reduce one source of variation but do not promise identical results on every device or kernel. Leakage checks should cover duplicates, temporal overlap, and target-derived features, not just a random split label.
lessons.whyItMatters: Reproducibility records and leakage audits solve different problems and both are needed.
